files.why: Add BillingPeriod entity (id, name, start, end) and a BillingPeriodSummary read model carrying per-period totals; billing is the slice this finance concept is about.
Add framework-free logic to test membership (invoice/appointment falls in the period's range) and sum invoice totals into per-period totals for the read model.
Add the server DTO for a billing period (snake_case keys, ISO date strings) with a zod schema, kept private to data/.
Map the billing-period DTO to/from the core entity so DTO shapes never leak upward.
Add fetchBillingPeriods/fetchBillingPeriodById and compose the period read model by joining its invoices with scheduling appointments via @slices/scheduling.
Seed billing-period rows and add MSW handlers for /api/billing-periods so the feature has mock data end to end.
Own the new /billing-periods and /billing-periods/:id route paths pointing at the new views.
Expose BillingPeriod type(s) and the period query on the slice's only public surface (routes are already re-exported).
List composable that loads periods with their totals for the list view.
Detail composable that assembles one period's invoices, its appointments (via scheduling's public API), and totals.
List page showing each named period and its total; the .vue must live under a slice's ui/ per the structure test.
Detail page showing the grouped appointments, invoices, and totals for a single period.
Add a date-range read model (fetchAppointmentsInRange) so billing can list the appointments that happened in a period; existing queries only cover a day or upcoming/by-id.
Export the new range read model on scheduling's public surface so billing joins it via @slices/scheduling, never a deep import.
Add a nav link so the new billing-periods pages are reachable (nav is an app/composition concern).
Add unit tests for period membership and per-period total math (core rules are tested by relative path here).
Add tests for the new billing-period DTO<->core mapping (round-trip, date parsing).

uncertain: Whether 'billing period' should be a new top-level slice instead of living in billing. I placed it in billing because the concept is named/finance-owned and grouping invoices is a billing concern; a new slice would edit the CODEOWNERS-protected architecture.config.ts `slices` array and trigger architecture review, which seems unwarranted. But it spans both invoices and appointments, so a reviewer could argue for its own slice.

How period membership is defined: by date range (appointment.start / invoice.issueDate inside the period) vs. an explicit period_id foreign key on invoices/appointments. I assumed date-range-derived, which is why I added a scheduling range query; if membership is an explicit id, the scheduling query and the join logic look different.

Whether per-period totals are computed client-side in core/rules from the member invoices, or come precomputed from the server DTO. I modeled core computing them; if the server owns the totals, core/rules changes shrink and dto/mappers grow.

Whether a dedicated BillingPeriodTotals.vue component is warranted or the totals should just render inline in the detail/list views (rule 6/7 — don't make a component without a distinct reason to change). Left it out of the firm list.
Whether periods have a lifecycle (open/closed/locked) needing billing/core/policy.ts (canClose, etc.) and a mutation in data/mutations.ts. Omitted pending the read-only-vs-editable answer.
Whether billing periods should also surface on the app ClientOverviewView; I did not include it since the request describes standalone period pages.
questions: Is a period's contents defined purely by its date range, or do invoices/appointments carry an explicit period assignment (period_id) that Finance sets? This decides the join strategy and the shape of the scheduling query.
Are the per-period totals authoritative from the backend, or should the frontend derive them by summing the invoices in the period?
Does Finance need to create/edit/open/close periods (a lifecycle + mutations), or is this read-only reporting for now?

Are periods scoped to a single client (like the current overview), or global across all clients? Totals across clients raise a mixed-currency question — how should we total periods that contain multiple currencies?
Which timestamp defines membership — invoice issue date vs. due date, and appointment start vs. end — and are period boundaries inclusive/exclusive?
Should billing periods appear in the top nav and/or the client overview, or only as their own dedicated pages?
